jobs.title: Senior Generative AI Engineer
jobs.jd: Senior Generative AI Engineer Background We are looking for a Senior Generative AI Engineer to design, build, and ship production-grade Generative AI and Agentic AI applications that delivery business value across the organization. This role is focused on building AI applications and services at scale. You will be responsible for building robust, secure, and highly scalable systems that integrate with leading cloud-based AI services. You will work alongside product managers, designers, and other engineers as an individual contributor. You are expected to own features end-to-end, and to deliver high-quality, reusable code that scales beyond a single use case. Key Responsibilities Software Engineering and Execution Design, build, and ship production-grade Generative and Agentic AI features and applications Own features end-to-end from technical design through implementation, testing, deployment and operation Build reusable, well-abstracted components and shared utilities (e.g., RAG building blocks, agent scaffolding, evaluation harnesses, prompt utilities) to enable faster delivery of future Generative and Agentic AI products Build multi-agent systems using frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, Claude Agent SDK and Google ADK Integrate with leading LLM and foundation model APIs, including Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, and AWS Bedrock Build Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, including document ingestion, chunking strategies, embeddings, vector search, and re-ranking Build clean, well-tested RESTful and/or gRPC APIs with a focus on reliability, security, and performance Implement observability, tracing, evaluation, guardrails for Generative and Agentic AI applications Deploy and operate services on major cloud providers (e.g., GCP, AWS, and Azure) leveraging managed services Participate actively in code reviews and design discussions, sharing knowledge with peers Required Qualifications 5-7 years of professional software engineering experience with at least 3 years of experience building AI/ML software products Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field (Master's degree preferred) Strong proficiency in Python, with deep software engineering fundamentals (abstraction, modularity, system design, testing, performance) Hands-on experience building and shipping Generative and Agentic AI applications, including LLM integration, prompt engineering, and/or agentic workflows Practical experience integrating cloud-hosted LLM APIs such as Azure OpenAI, Vertex AI, and/or AWS Bedrock Experience with agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, Google ADK, Claude Agent SDK) and vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, Open Search, AlloyDB) Hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Amazon Web Services (AWS), or Azure Solid understanding of API design, distributed systems, and cloud-native architecture Track record of taking systems from design through production deployment and operation Preferred Qualifications Experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) Knowledge of Generative AI Risk Management frameworks (NIST RFM) Experience supporting developer platforms or internal tooling Originally posted jobs.title: LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer
jobs.jd: Cos'è Blox Space ? Blox Space lavora al centro dell'economia tech,in partnership con un network di oltre 70 realtà attive nel mondo dell'AI, del software, della cybersecurity e delle Freedom Technologies, impegnate nello sviluppo di infrastrutture, prodotti e servizi legati all'economia digitale, alla data protection e al futuro del denaro. ﻿Aiutiamo a connettere i talenti con questo ecosistema, operando come Talent Bridge tra le ambizioni di crescita dei professionisti e le opportunità offerte dal nostro network. ﻿In questo momento stiamo supportando una delle nostre partner companies nella ricerca di un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer, e se pensi di essere il profilo giusto, ci piacerebbe conoscerti. Il Ruolo L'azienda è una startup di cybersecurity italiana che costruisce sistemi di sicurezza autonomi: individuano vulnerabilità sconosciute, prioritizzano il rischio reale e distribuiscono le correzioni senza intervento umano, con un focus sui binari compilati, perché è quello che gira davvero in produzione. È un team early, pre-seed, fondato da ricercatori di sicurezza e accademici di primo piano. ﻿Cerchiamo un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer che adatti, valuti e metta in produzione modelli linguistici open-weight, ma piegati a un unico scopo: trovare e capire vulnerabilità. Per questo cerchiamo una persona fortemente orientata alla cybersecurity, che non si limiti ad addestrare modelli ma capisca il dominio su cui lavorano. Non è un ruolo di prompt engineering: è l'intero ciclo di post-training, dal design dei dataset al fine tuning, dalla generazione di dati sintetici alla valutazione, fino al deploy in ambienti locali, privati o ristretti. ﻿ Non cerchiamo il curriculum perfetto, cerchiamo la testa giusta. Cerchiamo chi sa trasformare un foundation model in un sistema affidabile e specifico per il compito, sa quando il fine tuning è la strada giusta e quando invece conviene prompting, retrieval, orchestrazione o tooling, e porta con sé una vera sensibilità per il mindset di chi attacca. ﻿ Le responsabilità di un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer in questo contesto possono spaziare dal fine tuning e dall'adattamento di LLM open-weight per casi d'uso di sicurezza, interni o rivolti al cliente, al confronto tra approcci di post-training (SFT, tecniche parameter-efficient come LoRA e QLoRA, preference tuning come DPO dove serve, full fine tuning quando giustificato), dalla costruzione e pulizia di dataset di qualità e dalla generazione di dati sintetici alla definizione di metodi di valutazione che vanno oltre i benchmark generici, fino all'analisi di regressioni e failure mode e al lavoro con il team di engineering per servire i modelli in ambienti vincolati. ﻿﻿﻿ Le skill che fanno la differenza Esperienza pratica vera nel fine tuning di LLM: in produzione, in ricerca applicata o in contesti sperimentali seri, con più tecniche di post-training alle spalle, idealmente SFT, LoRA e QLoRA. Orientamento forte alla cybersecurity: capisci (o hai una gran voglia di capire a fondo) threat model, bug hunting e la logica di chi attacca. È il dominio su cui i modelli lavorano, e qui fa la differenza tra un buon fine tuning e uno inutile. Dati prima di tutto: sai costruire, curare e mantenere dataset per training e valutazione, e sai generare, filtrare e validare dati sintetici per migliorare il comportamento del modello, non per gonfiare le metriche. Stack solido: Python forte, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, tokenizzazione, preprocessing e training pipeline sono pane quotidiano. Dimestichezza con i vincoli reali: limiti di GPU, trade-off memoria/performance, workflow quantization-aware e ottimizzazione del training. Mentalità da debugging: sai capire perché un modello è migliorato, è regredito, ha fatto overfit o ha fallito, e la valutazione la imposti su quello che conta davvero a livello operativo, non sui punteggi generici. Autonomia a cavallo tra ricerca, dati ed engineering: ti muovi da solo su tutti e tre i fronti. Sono Very Nice to Have: un background in software security o vulnerability research, esperienza in CTF, deploy in ambienti air-gapped, on-premise o ristretti, inference optimization, quantization, model serving o runtime LLM locali, training distribuito o multi-GPU, eval harness, red-teaming o model safety testing. Ti manca qualcosa rispetto a quello che hai letto? Candidati comunque: siamo a caccia di game-changer, non di checklist da spuntare!﻿ Work arrangements Il ruolo ha come sede preferenziale l'hub di Blox Space a Torino, un ambiente cost-effective e ad alta densità di persone tecniche di valore, ma valutiamo candidature da tutta Italia, con modalità operative flessibili da concordare insieme al team. ﻿Per il ruolo è previsto un range retributivo di 40.000 – 60.000 € lordi annui, con la disponibilità a valutare anche proposte superiori per profili particolarmente senior o di valore eccezionale. ﻿Sono inoltre previsti un contributo di 1.000 € per il setup dell'home office, un piano AI premium a tua scelta e retreat aziendali in Italia. Unisciti all'ecosistema con Blox Space ! Se vuoi rendere i modelli open-weight davvero affidabili e utili contro uno dei problemi più difficili della sicurezza, e farlo accanto a chi trova bug veri in sistemi veri, questa è l'opportunità che stavi aspettando: lavorare con una delle nostre partner companies significa entrare in un team innovativo e in forte crescita, al centro di un ecosistema dove circolano idee, competenze e progetti ad alta intensità. È un ambiente dove si costruisce, si testa, si discute e si migliora ogni giorno. Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.title: AI Research Engineer
jobs.jd: At Dscout , we’re building the most flexible and powerful UX research platform on the market—trusted by the world’s top brands in finance (JP Morgan Chase, Intuit, Charles Schwab, PayPal), healthcare (Aya, Headspace), consumer goods (Keen, Verizon, Target, Northface), and tech (Google, Amazon, Facebook, Meta, Spotify, AirBnB). Our tools help teams deeply understand the humans behind their products, so they can build better ones. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us. At Dscout, we're building the human-grounded layer that teaches AI to work in the real world and proves it stays aligned there. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us. Dscout AI Training & Evals builds human data and evals that show whether AI works for real people. For ten years Dscout has captured how people behave in real context, with consent and scientific rigor. Dscout AI Training & Evals points that engine at AI: consented human behavior and judgment, turned into the training data, evals, and benchmarks AI teams trust. Models ace benchmarks and still surprise people in the wild. A benchmark says how capable a model is. It does not say whether the model works for the person using it, across weeks, in the mess of real life. That gap is where we work. We serve AI researchers, the product builders who ship alongside them, and the research teams who partner with both. We are a new unit inside an established company: live customers, a mature platform (React, Elixir, Python, Swift, Kotlin; SOC 2 and HITRUST certified), a small senior team, and room to build. We work AI-native. Agents write code, evals gate changes, and we aim to do in months what used to take years. A note from our Chief AI Officer & GM. The hardest AI problems show up when a model meets real people, with their tools, their interruptions, and their goals. Our customers need a partner who can design the answer, build it, and ship it fast. Ground Truth sits where deployment meets research: what we learn in the field shapes the science, and the science shapes what we ship. Come build it with us. Why this seat Work on a problem the field has not solved: measuring whether AI works for real people, over real time. Study something most evals do not have: real participants, doing real tasks in their own context. Own the benchmark. You are founding it, not joining a team that has one. Publish. Methods and benchmarks go to the research community, with first authorship on the benchmark. Join a small senior team with direct access to the Head of AI Research and the GM. This is a research-first role focused on questions where the right rubric, benchmark, or method does not yet exist. You will find the gaps, propose bold directions, and take projects from the first hypothesis through experiments and benchmark construction to publication. You will also build: the science has to run inside live customer programs. What you will do Rubrics and QA science Design rubrics and test whether they measure what they claim: validity, reliability, and sensitivity. Measure how reliable human raters are, and when disagreement is noise versus real signal. Calibrate AI judges against real human judgment, and study when they drift away from it. Build quality signals that put evidence behind every data point we ship. Long-horizon, real-user benchmarks Design Dscout’s first benchmark: real users, in real context, over long horizons. Multi-week tasks across tools, not one-shot prompts. Define the protocol, task design, scoring, and release. Work with our delivery team on fieldwork. Work out how to keep a living benchmark honest over time: drift, contamination, difficulty, and what counts as a meaningful change. Write the paper and own the public release. Human judgment as training and eval signal Study when real-world human feedback improves a model and when it adds noise. Explore how preference and judgment data from representative people differ from expert data. Turn findings into methods our forward deployed engineers and delivery team can run in the field. New research directions These areas are the core, not the whole list. You will have significant latitude to propose new programs, such as calibrating user simulations against real behavior, human-AI collaboration, and behavioral evaluation of agents. Co-author with outside labs and academics on studies that need real-user data. Help run our paper-reading group. A good first year A QA and rubric framework running on live customer programs, with documented validity. Benchmark v0 released, with a paper submitted to a top venue. At least one external team using or citing our work. Delivery colleagues using your methods without needing you in the room. How we will hire: a conversation with the Head of AI Research; a research talk on your publication; a design exercise (how would you validate a rubric for a long-horizon task?); a conversation with the GM, forward deployed engineers, and delivery partners. What we care about most. A strong publication record helps. We care most about whether you can find the question that matters, design a rigorous way to answer it, and move fast enough that the answer is still useful. What you bring Published research in evals, preference learning, reward modeling, human-AI interaction, measurement, or agent evaluation. A PhD, a PhD in progress, or an MS with two or more strong research internships at labs or top industry groups. If you do not have advanced degrees but have a history of creative machine learning research work, this is just as desirable. Strong applied statistics: inter-rater reliability, confidence intervals, power, and a nose for when a metric misleads. Hands-on experience with LLM-as-judge, rubric-based evaluation, and preference data. Strong Python, and the ability to build research prototypes and evaluation pipelines other people run. jobs.title: AI Forward Deployed Engineer - France
jobs.jd:
AI Engineer - FDE (Forward Deployed Engineer)

Req ID: CSQ427R334

We welcome remote applicants located near our offices. Preferred locations: Paris, France. Remote location for candidates to be based in the France region only (not remote from any other country)

Mission

The AI Forward Deployed Engineering (AI FDE) team is a highly specialised customer-facing AI team at Databricks. We deliver professional services engagements to help our customers build and productionize first-of-its-kind AI applications. We work cross-functionally to shape long-term strategic priorities and initiatives alongside engineering, product, and developer relations, as well as support internal subject matter expert (SME) teams. We view our team as an ensemble: we look for individuals with strong, unique specialisations to improve the overall strength of the team. This team is the right fit for you if you love working with customers, teammates, and fueling your curiosity for the latest trends in GenAI, LLMOps, and ML more broadly.

Reporting to: Senior Manager - AI FDE, EMEA

The impact you will have:

  • Develop cutting-edge GenAI solutions, incorporating the latest techniques from Databricks AI research to solve customer problems
  • Own production rollouts of consumer and internally facing GenAI applications
  • Serve as a trusted technical advisor to customers across a variety of domains
  • Present at conferences such as Data + AI Summit, recognized as a thought leader internally and externally
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with the product and engineering teams to influence priorities and shape the product roadmap 

What we look for:

  • Min 4 years' experience 
  • Experience building GenAI applications, including RAG, multi-agent systems, Text2SQL, fine-tuning, etc., with tools such as HuggingFace, LangChain, and DSPy
  • Expertise in deploying production-grade GenAI applications, including evaluation and optimisations 
  • Extensive years of hands-on industry data science experience, leveraging common machine learning and data science tools, i.e. pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch, etc.
  • Experience building production-grade machine learning deployments on AWS, Azure, or GCP
  • Graduate degree in a quantitative discipline (Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Operations Research, etc.) or equivalent practical experience
  • Experience communicating and/or teaching technical concepts to non-technical and technical audiences alike
  • Passion for collaboration, life-long learning, and driving business value through AI
  • [Preferred] Experience using the Databricks Intelligence Platform and Apache Spark™ to process large-scale distributed datasets
  • Willing to travel once every 4-8 weeks to see customers (as needed)

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. jobs.jd:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data scientists and data analysts learn and grow together. The Treasury Finance Data Science team builds the models, risk frameworks, and decision tools behind how Stripe manages money at global scale: liquidity, funding, counterparty risk, and foreign exchange.

Stripe moves funds across 135+ currencies every day. That creates FX exposure from merchant flows, multi-currency balances, and entity funding. In this role, you'll be a thought partner and builder alongside Stripe's FX team. Together you'll develop the quantitative foundation for how Stripe measures, forecasts, and hedges FX exposure.

What you'll do

You'll be the senior quantitative lead for FX within Treasury Finance Data Science. You'll co-build with Treasury, the FX hedging team, Finance, and Engineering: shaping the research agenda, turning ideas into rigorous models, and building the systems that put those models to work. Data Science owns these systems. They produce the decision-critical outputs and analyses that the FX team and Treasury leadership rely on. This is a hands-on role. jobs.title: Founding ML Engineer (Spectrum)
jobs.jd:
Software engineers and AI agents alike suffer from the same problem: finding that one person or place that will answer their tough, specific question. Many solutions promise to solve this with similarity search in vector databases. Unfortunately, finding the answer is often a puzzle with pieces to be collected across a myriad of contradictory sources and cannot be solved without surgical search and careful reasoning. 

Spectrum collects data from an organization’s code, docs, and issues, and organizes knowledge in a unified ontology that AI agents can efficiently search through and reason over. We aim to revolutionize the semantic layer space for software-building organizations and move beyond specs that fall out of sync with code, introducing a living spec – one that’s extracted from the whole system and used to keep it aligned. Spectrum is meant to be the single source of truth for all product and architectural knowledge.

Spectrum is a resident of JetBrains' startup incubator, with startup speed and autonomy, and backed by 25 years of developer tooling expertise. We are looking for a top-class ML Engineer who will help us shape the future of software development. You will own our AI and ML engineering stack and help define the research agenda for our team. Your technical vision and design decisions will directly shape the product and determine its success.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Designing and building the ML/LLM solution for data ingestion, knowledge extraction, retrieval, and subsequent reasoning.
  • Creating the datasets, metrics, and pipelines that drive measurable improvements across the system.
  • Architecting and improving agents for context retrieval, knowledge extraction, and data alignment, which includes prompt engineering, model selection, and inference optimization.
  • Establishing MLOps practices, including orchestration, observability, and experiment tracking.
  • Collaborating with the engineering team on system design and with JetBrains Research on the research agenda.
  • Defining hiring criteria, growing the ML team, and shaping the ML team culture.

We expect you to have:

  • A proven track record as an ML/AI Lead.
  • At least five years of experience in ML/AI systems, with at least two years focused on LLMs and generative AI.
  • A deep understanding of the LLM ecosystem, including model architectures and fine-tuning approaches.
  • Hands-on experience with:
    • Prompt engineering and LLM pipeline design, including evaluation.
    • Agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangSmith, smolagents, or an equivalent.
    • Vector databases and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns.
    • Deploying and scaling LLM-powered applications using APIs (e.g. OpenAI or Anthropic) or open-source models.
  • Strong Python skills – Kotlin knowledge would be a plus.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to diverse audiences.
  • Proficiency in English, both written and verbal. 

Our ideal candidate would have:

  • Experience with ontologies, knowledge graphs, or graph-based reasoning.
  • Experience in early-stage startups – you enjoy the zero-to-one phase.
  • The ability to think strategically about product-led AI, beyond just training models in isolation.
  • A background in code analysis, developer tools, or software engineering research.
  • Experience with multi-agent systems or complex agentic workflows.
  • Actively contributed to relevant open-source projects or publications.

What we offer

  • A competitive salary and JetBrains benefits.
  • A generous runway and corporate resources with startup autonomy.

Our work spans personalized Search, music video discovery and ranking, audiobook Search expansion, and the foundations of more social Search experiences. The AI Forward Deployed Engineering (AI FDE) team is a highly specialized customer-facing AI team at Databricks. We deliver professional services engagements to help our customers build and productionize first-of-its-kind AI applications. We work cross-functionally to shape long-term strategic priorities and initiatives alongside engineering, product, and developer relations, as well as support internal subject matter expert (SME) teams.   • Present at conferences such as Data + AI Summit, recognized as a thought leader internally and externally

jobs.title: Data Scientist, FX Quantitative Research
jobs.jd:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data scientists and data analysts learn and grow together. The Treasury Finance Data Science team builds the models, risk frameworks, and decision tools behind how Stripe manages money at global scale: liquidity, funding, counterparty risk, and foreign exchange.

Stripe moves funds across 135+ currencies every day. That creates FX exposure from merchant flows, multi-currency balances, and entity funding. In this role, you'll be a thought partner and builder alongside Stripe's FX team. Together you'll develop the quantitative foundation for how Stripe measures, forecasts, and hedges FX exposure.

What you'll do

You'll be the senior quantitative lead for FX within Treasury Finance Data Science. You'll co-build with Treasury, the FX hedging team, Finance, and Engineering: shaping the research agenda, turning ideas into rigorous models, and building the systems that put those models to work. Data Science owns these systems. They produce the decision-critical outputs and analyses that the FX team and Treasury leadership rely on. This is a hands-on role. You'll design the methodology, write the code, and ship it into production.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with the FX team to build and evolve FX risk measurement: exposure aggregation across entities and currencies, VaR / Expected Shortfall, stress testing, and scenario analysis
  • Develop forecasting models for FX exposures and multi-currency cash flows. Quantify forecast uncertainty so it can inform hedge sizing and timing.
  • Co-design hedge optimization and decision frameworks with the FX team that weigh hedge cost, residual risk, P&L volatility, and liquidity constraints
  • Build ML and statistical systems for trading and risk (signal research, anomaly detection on flows, execution and cost analytics), and take them from prototype to production
  • Own the production systems that generate decision-critical FX outputs, partnering with Engineering on reliability, SLAs, monitoring, alerting, and incident response for risk-critical workflows
  • Partner deeply with Treasury Finance stakeholders to turn business questions into quantitative frameworks. Anticipate needs and help shape FX risk strategy rather than reacting to requests.
  • Produce clear, trusted analyses and reporting that inform Treasury and Finance leadership decisions, including leadership-level reporting such as MBRs and QBRs
  • Use AI tools (code assistants, LLM-based agents) to speed up modeling, analysis, and automation, while maintaining rigor, validation, and auditability
  • Raise the technical bar for FX quantitative work within Data Science: methodology standards, model validation, documentation, and mentoring other data scientists

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • BS/BA with 8+ years, MS/MA with 6+ years, or PhD with 3+ years of full-time experience in quantitative finance, risk modeling, quantitative research, or data science
  • Hands-on quantitative experience at a bank, asset manager, hedge fund, trading firm, or similar financial institution, with direct exposure to FX, rates, or market risk
  • Strong foundation in statistics, probability, and time-series modeling, plus working knowledge of risk measures (VaR, Expected Shortfall, stress testing) and hedging instruments (forwards, swaps, options)
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL. You write production-quality code, not just research scripts.
  • Experience taking models or analytical systems from research into production
  • Business acumen and the ability to turn complex analyses into clear, decision-ready insights
  • Ability to clearly communicate results and drive impact with cross-functional partners, including senior non-technical stakeholders
  • Ability to manage multiple projects at once, with strong attention to detail
  • Experience using AI tools to speed up modeling, analysis, and coding

Preferred qualifications

  • MS or PhD in a quantitative field (e.g., Quantitative / Mathematical Finance, Financial Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research)
  • Applied machine learning experience in trading or risk (e.g., forecasting, execution analytics, signal research, anomaly detection)
  • Experience with corporate treasury or balance-sheet FX: multi-entity exposure management, hedge programs, and treasury concepts such as liquidity, funding, and cash positioning
  • Experience building risk or decision systems with engineering standards: code review, testing, monitoring, and defined SLAs
  • Experience with distributed data tools (e.g., Spark) and workflow orchestration (e.g., Airflow, Flyte)
  • Prior experience at a growth-stage internet, fintech, or payments company
  • Experience creating leadership-level reporting, such as QBRs and MBRs

jobs.jd: Are you passionate about working with Amazon-scale data, advanced analytics, and data science? Does the idea of working closely with a team of highly experience machine-learning scientists and engineers excite you? If you like working with data and want to harness the power of it to develop a deeper understanding of customer behaviour, identify opportunities, impact publishing workflow and influence the business strategy to develop products and features that have a direct impact on the creator and reader experience, this is the role for you! Key job responsibilities As Data Scientist, you will connect with world leaders in your field working on similar problems. You will be working with massive-scale data and providing analytic leadership to scientists, product managers, engineers using these data. jobs.title: AI/ML Engineer
jobs.jd: About the Singapore AI Center of Excellence (COE) The Singapore AI Center of Excellence (COE) is a dedicated engineering and R&D hub focused on Enterprise and Sovereign AI. Our mission is to help organizations move AI workflows cleanly into production through two main paths: creating reusable software architectures that solve common industry problems, and contributing code directly to upstream open-source projects to fix enterprise gaps in system deployment, runtime tuning, and platform management. Basing our engineering team in Singapore creates a close feedback loop between customers, partners, and core product teams. This direct connection keeps our development roadmaps relevant, speeds up solution delivery, and strengthens our ability to co-innovate across the region. Role Overview The AI/ML Engineer is a highly technical, hands-on role at the intersection of Enterprise AI and client-facing architecture. As part of our Customer Engineering function, you will write production-grade solution blueprints alongside strategic customers and technology partners. Your mission is to solve immediate, high-stakes operational bottlenecks in the APAC region by delivering repeatable, extensible, and open-sourced AI Quickstarts that show the industry how to solve complex challenges. In this team, career growth and seniority are defined purely by your technical competence, architectural depth, and ability to deliver end-to-end solutions autonomously in highly ambiguous environments. There is no expectation of team management, project coordination, or formal talent mentorship; your progression is driven entirely by engineering impact. What You Will Do: Enterprise-Minded Blueprinting: Design and build comprehensive, production-ready architecture blueprints and reference codebases. These blueprints must naturally take into account critical enterprise requirements—including systems-level hardening, infrastructure scalability, and network isolation boundaries—without you needing to perform the last-mile hands-on production deployment yourself. Open-Source AI Quickstarts: Package repeatable, extensible technical architectures as open-sourced AI Quickstarts to solve complex, real-world industry problems and accelerate ecosystem adoption. Co-Development & Integration: Collaborate with external engineering teams (such as semiconductor partners, regional AI programs, and software vendors) to validate joint-architecture blueprints, ensuring stable integrations across the system stack. Benchmarking & Evaluation: Design and integrate automated testing, evaluation harnesses, and system-level telemetry into blueprints to monitor and measure performance metrics like latency, throughput, cost, and model quality. Regulated & Secure Design: Proactively incorporate robust data privacy standards, secure network perimeters, and localized hosting considerations into all solution blueprints to satisfy compliance and risk management requirements in highly regulated environments. What You Will Bring: Academic & Professional Experience Education: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related quantitative field. Software Engineering Foundations: Excellent understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including clean code principles, test-driven development (TDD), CI/CD automation pipelines, and version control (Git) workflows. Communication: Clear verbal and written communication skills in English, with the ability to articulate complex technical architectures to other engineers and technical stakeholders. Core Technical Stack Programming Languages: Exceptional, hands-on proficiency in Python (specifically for machine learning and systems programming). Solid familiarity with lower-level system languages such as Go or C/C++ is highly preferred. Deep Learning & ML Libraries: Strong familiarity with PyTorch and core NLP/vision ecosystems (e.g., Hugging Face Transformers, datasets, and tokenizers). Cloud-Native Frameworks: Strong practical experience deploying containerized applications on Kubernetes or production-grade enterprise container orchestration platforms. Base MLOps Knowledge: Conceptual and hands-on understanding of model serving lifecycles, data ingestion steps, and automated packaging. Target Knowledge Domains & Growth Areas We are building a multi-disciplinary engineering squad. Candidates are expected to bring experience in some of the following domains, and will have the opportunity to continuously develop their skills across all of them as they grow in seniority: Platform & Pipeline Engineering: Experience with distributed computing frameworks and cluster schedulers (such as Ray), workflow orchestration (such as MLflow or Kubeflow), distributed unstructured data parsing tools (such as Docling), and vector database structures. Generative AI & Agentic Architectures: Familiarity with LLM orchestration engines (such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or LangGraph), agentic workflows (AgentOps), tool-calling protocols (such as Model Context Protocol) and model fine-tuning (PEFT/SFT). Hardware Heterogeneity & Runtime Optimization: Understanding of model serving runtimes (such as vLLM), optimizing engines for latency and throughput (e.g., KV cache offloading, chunked prefill), and running benchmarks across diverse hardware setups including CUDA, ROCm, and emerging GPU/NPU architectures. Regulated Deployments: Designing isolated, air-gapped container networks, secure registry services, and local inference environments to meet strict data residency, privacy, and compliance policies. Nice-to-Have: Industry Domain Experience While not strictly required, experience applying AI/ML architectures to solve challenges in the following regulated industries is a strong advantage: Financial Services (FSI): Familiarity with risk-assessment models, fraud detection patterns, or compliance requirements under regulatory frameworks. Public Sector & Healthcare: Experience handling highly sensitive or anon

jobs.title: Medior AI Engineer
jobs.jd: Van slimme AI-modellen naar oplossingen die écht werken. Een AI-model bouwen is één ding. Zorgen dat het betrouwbaar draait, gekoppeld is aan echte data en waarde toevoegt bij een klant: daar wordt het interessant. Bij adesso werk je aan AI-oplossingen die verder gaan dan experimenten, van machine learning en MLOps tot generatieve AI, LLM's en agents. Je bouwt, implementeert en verbetert oplossingen die organisaties echt gebruiken. Wat ga je doen? Als Medior AI Engineer werk je samen met senior AI Engineers en Forward Deployed Engineers aan klantprojecten. Je pakt zelfstandig onderdelen op en groeit in architectuur en end-to-end verantwoordelijkheid. AI ontwikkelen: je bouwt ML-modellen, LLM-toepassingen en agentic workflows. Van idee naar productie: je bouwt data- en ML-pipelines, automatiseert deployments en zorgt voor monitoring en betrouwbaarheid. Slim integreren: je koppelt AI aan bestaande systemen, API's en cloud- en dataplatformen. Meedenken met de klant: je vertaalt vraagstukken naar praktische, schaalbare oplossingen. Kennis delen: je legt herbruikbare patronen vast en deelt wat je leert met je collega's. Projecten die verder gaan dan het model We richten ons op retail en e-commerce, finance en utilities. Denk aan: Prognoses waar planners op durven te sturen, van retailassortiment tot netbelasting. Intelligente documentverwerking, zoals KYC-dossiers of inspectierapporten, met herleidbare bronnen. Agents die werk voorbereiden in klantenservice en backoffice, met evals en guardrails. Computer vision, zoals in de fitnessbranche, waar we onveilige situaties in onbemande 24/7-locaties herkennen. De uitdaging zit niet alleen in het model, maar ook in betrouwbaarheid, integratie en de werking in de praktijk. Je kiest steeds de techniek die bij het probleem past. Wat breng je mee? Ervaring met het ontwikkelen en in productie brengen van ML- of GenAI-oplossingen. Goede kennis van Python, SQL en machine learning. Ervaring met MLOps en/of LLM's, RAG en AI-agents. Kennis van minimaal één cloudplatform (Azure, AWS of GCP) en een dataplatform zoals Databricks, Snowflake of Fabric. Je werkt met coding agents en beoordeelt kritisch wat ze opleveren. Je denkt vanuit de klantvraag en legt technische keuzes helder uit. Je spreekt en schrijft vloeiend Nederlands en Engels. Wat dit níet is Geen individuele detachering. Je werkt aan projecten namens adesso, met een team achter je. Geen notebook-kerkhof. Een model is pas af als het in productie draait en gebruikt wordt. Geen GenAI omdat het kan. Soms is een klassiek model beter, soms een LLM; jij kiest wat past. Geen werk op afroep. Je denkt vanaf de klantvraag mee, niet pas als het ontwerp al vastligt. Het team Je wordt onderdeel van ons AI Engineering-team: AI engineering consultants in twee rollen. De Forward Deployed AI Engineer (FDE) is eigenaar van het klantprobleem en ontwerpt de oplossing, inclusief de agentic architectuur. Jij gaat als AI Engineer de diepte in op bouw, data, MLOps en schaal, en denkt vanaf de klantvraag mee over de juiste aanpak. Je krijgt ruimte om je eigen werk vorm te geven, maar je bent nooit alleen verantwoordelijk voor alle specialismen. Heb je diepe kennis van finance, retail of utilities en wil je dichter op de klant zitten? Kijk dan ook naar onze FDE-vacatures. Twijfel je? Solliciteer dan gewoon; we kijken samen welke rol het best past. Waarom adesso? Omdat je bij ons écht kunt meebouwen. Bij adesso Nederland draait het om meer dan alleen technologie. We bouwen slimme oplossingen die daadwerkelijk waarde toevoegen voor onze klanten. Geen eindeloze experimenten of AI omdat het hip is, maar technologie die werkt en impact maakt. We zijn onderdeel van de internationale adesso Group, met ruim 11.500 collega's op meer dan 60 locaties. Tegelijkertijd zijn we in Nederland een relatief klein en persoonlijk team, met korte lijnen, veel vrijheid en ruimte voor eigen initiatief. Groot genoeg om impact te maken, klein genoeg om het verschil te voelen. AI-native: wij omarmen AI, ook in ons eigen werk We geloven dat AI fundamenteel verandert hoe we software bouwen, met data werken en klanten helpen. Daarom bouwen we niet aan losse experimenten, maar aan dataplatformen, AI-first applicaties en agentic oplossingen die echt onderdeel worden van bedrijfsprocessen. Dat geldt ook voor hoe we zelf werken. Met onze Agentic Delivery-aanpak en eigen tools kun je echt vliegen: Context en kennisbank: agents werken met wat er écht speelt bij de klant, en kennis en beslissingen blijven herleidbaar voor mens én agent. AgentOps en governance: zicht op wat agents doen en controle over wat ze mogen, zodat ze veilig en binnen de regels werken. adSCAILE: ons eigen framework waarmee je samen met AI-agents bouwt, geïntegreerd, veilig en traceerbaar, in cycli van twee tot vier dagen in plaats van sprints van weken. Je gebruikt deze tools dagelijks en helpt ze verder te ontwikkelen. adesso is bovendien Select Partner in het Claude Partner Network van Anthropic. En we blijven kritisch: niet alles hoeft met AI. De beste oplossing staat altijd voorop. En misschien wel het belangrijkste: de mensen Je komt terecht in een team waar vakmanschap, ondernemerschap en kennisdeling centraal staan. Je werkt met ervaren specialisten en groeit richting architectuur en end-to-end verantwoordelijkheid. We houden van collega's die nieuwsgierig zijn, kennis delen en elkaar verder helpen. Mensen die goed zijn in hun vak, maar ook plezier hebben in samenwerken. Je krijgt bij ons vertrouwen, verantwoordelijkheid en de vrijheid om ideeën daadwerkelijk uit te voeren. jobs.title: Machine Learning Data Scientist posting
jobs.jd: Role summary: At Differential Bio, our mission is to unlock the potential of the bioeconomy by fixing how biological R&D and scale-up are done. We’re looking for a Machine Learning Data Scientist to join our growing cutting-edge modelling team. You will develop novel machine learning algorithms and mechanistic models of bioprocess systems and push them from research proof-of-concept into production-ready commercial use. This role is focused on research , including creating hybrid models that combine mechanistic and machine learning approaches to predict how microbial fermentations behave , and that keep working when we move to a new organism, a new sensor, or a larger reactor. You’ll play an instrumental role on two existing grants and work with leading academic groups and industrial partners on pilot- and production-scale data. In addition, you’ll develop new research projects and drive them to completion and application on customer projects. We’re interested in researchers who want their work to end up in real bioreactors and are excited about working at an early-stage startup. You should be comfortable owning hard, open-ended problems where nobody has the answer yet, making evidence-based decisions under uncertainty, and shipping real solutions. How you’ll work You’ll collaborate with technical leads and academic/industry external partners to design and execute research that meets our commitments in both consortia and strengthens our own platform. You’ll own your research projects from scoping to delivery, with support from our modelling lead but with autonomy and independence. You’ll work closely with our wet lab, dry lab and software teams, and identify which data you need to generate from our robotic lab. Key responsibilities: Hybrid bioprocess modelling Develop hybrid mechanistic/ML cell response models that predict fermentation outcomes (growth, titer, yield, productivity) from process and sensor data. Fuse time-series signals from process analytical technology (Raman, NIR, dielectric spectroscopy, dissolved oxygen, off-gas) with offline analytics. Build mechanistic backbones (e.g., kinetic/ODE models, genome-scale metabolic models) that constrain learning and generate synthetic training data. Develop machine learning surrogate models for computationally costly mechanistic simulations. Quantify uncertainty so that models can be trusted in high-stakes production settings. Transfer across organisms and scales Design models that carry over from benchtop to pilot and production scale, and across various microbes including bacteria and yeast. Use transfer learning and representation learning to make good predictions for new strains and processes with little data. Develop scale-transferable reactor characterisations and predictive KPI models for scale-up. Real-time Model-Predictive Control Build the AI/ML layer for Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and reinforcement-learning-based feeding strategies to optimize titer, rate, and yield dynamically. Fuse real-time data from Process Analytical Technology (PAT) and soft sensors (e.g., Raman, NIR) into dynamic state estimators to drive closed-loop bioreactor actuators (feed, air, agitation). Prototype simpler, deployable steps along the way, such as deviation detection and operator alerts Design control frameworks to proactively resolve metabolic bottlenecks and robustly account for model uncertainty, batch-to-batch variability, and inherent bioprocess stochasticity. Qualifications: PhD in machine learning, bioengineering, computational biology, or a related field, or a Master’s degree with 3+ years of relevant industry experience. Strong research independence; ability to scope and execute novel scientific work from start to finish. Demonstrated evidence of research contributions, including (but not limited to): peer-reviewed journal or conference papers, conference attendance, open-source contributions. Strong Python and modern ML tooling (e.g., PyTorch/JAX, scikit-learn). Hands-on experience building models of dynamical systems or time-series data, ideally combining mechanistic and data-driven approaches. Experience working with frontier coding models, including multi-agent orchestration. Clear written and verbal communication, including with non-ML partners. Nice-to-have: Experience with bioprocess or fermentation data, ideally from bioreactors at more than one scale Experience with Raman, NIR, or other spectroscopic data and chemometrics (e.g., PLS) Background in model-predictive control, reinforcement learning, or optimal control Experience with transfer learning, domain adaptation, or representation learning on biological data Familiarity with genome-scale metabolic models or kinetic modelling Experience with Bayesian methods, uncertainty quantification, or design of experiments Experience in collaborative or publicly funded research projects (e.g. Horizon Europe, Eurostars) Benefits: Competitive compensation through salary + stock options; we are looking to build a small but mighty team and think about compensation along those lines; Build your research profile: Work on open problems with leading European academic and industrial partners, with the intention to present and publish your work; A beautiful office in the heart of Munich, or remote work option with occasional travel eGym WellPass membership Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Digital Natives
jobs.jd: About the Team OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere. About the Role As an Applied AI Engineer, you will partner directly with Digital Native companies to design, build and deploy AI-powered products and systems. Working alongside customer product and engineering teams, you will take ideas from early experimentation through evaluation, production launch and scale, connecting technical decisions to user experience and measurable business impact. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve. This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees In this role, you will: - Partner directly with Digital Native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria. - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes. - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators. - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance. - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution. - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact. - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback. - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments. You’ll thrive in this role if you: - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting. - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering—not only program or stakeholder management. - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable. - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment. - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost. - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes. - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives. - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments. - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required. jobs.title: Senior ML Engineer (AI Research)
jobs.jd:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

This role is for Nebius AI R&D, a team focused on applied research in AI. Examples of applied research that we have recently published include:

  • applying reinforcement learning for agent training in long-context multi-turn scenarios
  • dramatically scaling task data collection to power reinforcement learning for SWE agents
  • building a decontaminated evaluation for SWE agents that is regularly updated
  • investigating how test-time guided search can be used to build more powerful agents

The results often lead to collaboration with adjacent teams where our research findings are applied in practice.

We are currently looking for senior- and staff-level ML engineers to work on research in areas such as:

  • Guided search and reinforcement learning for agentic systems
  • Reinforcement learning for reasoning models
  • Web-scale problem collection for training agents
  • Efficient model distillation

Some examples of what your responsibilities might include are:

  • Conducting experiments to figure out efficient ways to train a large language model on traces of interactions with various environments
  • Exploring methods of guided generation and search in the trajectory space
  • Coming up with ways to mine relevant data at web scale and figuring out efficient ways to use this data in model post-training
  • Conducting experiments with different reinforcement learning configurations in verifiable domains
  • Exploring methods to train AI agents on tasks with non-verifiable reward signals

We expect you to have:

  • A profound understanding of theoretical foundations of machine learning and reinforcement learning
  • Deep expertise in modern deep learning for language processing and generation
  • Substantial experience with training large models on multiple computational nodes
  • Strong software engineering skills (we mostly use python)
  • Deep experience with modern deep learning frameworks (we use jax)
  • Strong communication and leadership abilities
  • Experience designing, executing, and analyzing machine learning experiments with proper statistical rigor
  • Ability to formulate research questions, design experiments to test hypotheses, and draw meaningful conclusions from results
  • Ability to document research findings clearly and contribute to technical publications or report

Nice to have:

  • Experience with deep reinforcement learning for LLMs, including techniques such as reward modeling, DPO, PPO etc
  • Familiarity with important ideas in LLM space, such as RoPE, ZeRO/FSDP, Flash Attention, quantization
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related field Master’s or PhD preferred
  • Track record of building and delivering products (not necessarily ML-related) in a dynamic startup-like environment
  • Experience in engineering complex systems, such as large distributed data processing systems or high-load web services
  • Open-source projects that showcase your engineering prowess
  • Excellent command of the English language, alongside superior writing, articulation, and communication skills
  • Proficiency in contemporary software engineering approaches, including CI/CD, version control and unit testing

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI 

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire. 

If you need accommodations during the application process, please let us know.

NVIDIA is in a unique position: we develop AI-based products across multiple domains and collaborate with the world’s leading AI companies as partners and customers. This role is directed at measuring improving the security, content safety, and inclusivity of our frontier models. Because we are expanding across multiple pillars of safety, we are looking for specialists with deep expertise in one or more of the following core focus areas: LLM Security: Focus on backdoors, data poisoning, latent malicious behavior, and structural model vulnerabilities. Frontier Risks: Focus on advanced alignment challenges, including model deception, manipulation, and loss-of-control scenarios. Agentic Safety: Focus on LLM-level safety for autonomous systems, including multi-turn tool-calling, orchestration, and execution risks. Multi-turn Safety Evaluation: Focus on robust, scalable automated evaluation methodologies for conversational and iterative multi-turn use cases. What you'll be doing: Evaluation: Develop datasets and specialized models & algorithms to evaluate/benchmark models & end-to-end systems in our core safety tracks (LLM Security, Agentic Safety, Content Safety, Hallucinations, and ML Fairness). Model Pre-Training, Mid-Training, Post-Training: Develop datasets and recipes for filtering training data, developing training datasets & recipes, including components like RL environments and teacher models, across our core safety tracks (LLM Security, Agentic Safety, Content Safety, Hallucinations, and ML Fairness). Post-Training Experience: 4+ years of hands-on work experience in post-training of LLMs, including Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Reinforcement Learning (RLHF/RLAIF), safety data generation techniques, ablation studies, and deploying models to production. Frontier Risks (deception, manipulation, loss-of-control). Agentic Safety (LLM-level risks for multi-turn tool-calling/agents). jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer
jobs.jd: Jij zet AI-projecten op vanuit de inhoud en leidt ze tot een tevreden klant. Een sterk model bouwen is één ding. Een klant laten zien wat AI voor hem kan doen, de juiste oplossing bedenken en die betrouwbaar in productie krijgen: dat is jouw vak. Als Senior AI Engineer combineer je diepgang in machine learning en MLOps met diepgang in generatieve AI, LLM's en agents. Je bent erbij vanaf het eerste klantgesprek en bent als delivery lead eindverantwoordelijk voor de oplevering. Wat ga je doen? Nieuwe projecten opzetten: van eerste gesprek tot proposal, met steun van sales. Je inspireert de klant vanuit de inhoud, bedenkt de oplossing en zet een degelijke projectplanning neer. De oplevering leiden: als delivery lead doe je het projectmanagement, geef je dagelijks leiding aan de uitvoering en voer je het stakeholdermanagement. Technische keuzes maken en meebouwen: je ontwerpt de architectuur van data-, ML- en agentsystemen en bouwt zelf mee. Met een FDE in het team werk je het agentic ontwerp samen uit. Naar productie en draaiend houden: MLOps, monitoring, security en onderhoudbaarheid zijn bij jou geen bijzaak. Het team optillen: je begeleidt collega's en helpt standaarden te ontwikkelen. Projecten die verder gaan dan het model We richten ons op retail en e-commerce, finance en utilities. Denk aan: Prognoses waar planners op durven te sturen, van retailassortiment tot netbelasting. Intelligente documentverwerking, zoals KYC-dossiers of inspectierapporten, met herleidbare bronnen. Agents die werk voorbereiden in klantenservice en backoffice, met evals en guardrails. Computer vision, zoals in de fitnessbranche, waar we onveilige situaties in onbemande 24/7-locaties herkennen. De uitdaging zit niet alleen in het model, maar ook in betrouwbaarheid, integratie en de werking in de praktijk. Wat breng je mee? Diepgang in ML engineering en MLOps én in GenAI, LLM's en agents, met oplossingen die je zelf in productie hebt gebracht en onderhouden. Je ontwerpt de architectuur van data-, ML- en agentsystemen, met oog voor evals, monitoring, security en de EU AI Act. Sterk in Python en SQL, en hands-on met minimaal één cloud (Azure, AWS of GCP) en een dataplatform zoals Databricks, Snowflake of Fabric. Ervaring met business development én als delivery lead of projectleider. Je werkt dagelijks met coding agents en beoordeelt kritisch wat ze opleveren. Je spreekt en schrijft vloeiend Nederlands en Engels. Wat dit níet is Geen individuele detachering. Je werkt aan projecten namens adesso, met een team achter je. Geen notebook-kerkhof. Een model is pas af als het in productie draait en gebruikt wordt. Geen GenAI omdat het kan. Soms is een klassiek model beter, soms een LLM; jij kiest wat past. Geen werk op afroep. Je denkt vanaf de klantvraag mee, niet pas als het ontwerp al vastligt. Het team Je wordt onderdeel van ons AI Engineering-team: AI engineering consultants in twee rollen. De Forward Deployed AI Engineer (FDE) is eigenaar van het klantprobleem en ontwerpt de oplossing, inclusief de agentic architectuur. De AI Engineer gaat de diepte in op bouw, data, MLOps en schaal, en denkt vanaf de klantvraag mee over de juiste aanpak. Je krijgt ruimte om je eigen werk vorm te geven, maar je bent nooit alleen verantwoordelijk voor alle specialismen. Twijfel je welke rol het best bij je past? Solliciteer dan gewoon; we kijken samen. Waarom adesso? Omdat je bij ons écht kunt meebouwen. Bij adesso Nederland draait het om meer dan alleen technologie. We bouwen slimme oplossingen die daadwerkelijk waarde toevoegen voor onze klanten. Geen eindeloze experimenten of AI omdat het hip is, maar technologie die werkt en impact maakt. We zijn onderdeel van de internationale adesso Group, met ruim 11.500 collega's op meer dan 60 locaties. Tegelijkertijd zijn we in Nederland een relatief klein en persoonlijk team, met korte lijnen, veel vrijheid en ruimte voor eigen initiatief. Groot genoeg om impact te maken, klein genoeg om het verschil te voelen. AI-native: wij omarmen AI, ook in ons eigen werk We geloven dat AI fundamenteel verandert hoe we software bouwen, met data werken en klanten helpen. Daarom bouwen we niet aan losse experimenten, maar aan dataplatformen, AI-first applicaties en agentic oplossingen die echt onderdeel worden van bedrijfsprocessen. Dat geldt ook voor hoe we zelf werken. Met onze Agentic Delivery-aanpak en eigen tools kun je echt vliegen: Context en kennisbank: agents werken met wat er écht speelt bij de klant, en kennis en beslissingen blijven herleidbaar voor mens én agent. AgentOps en governance: zicht op wat agents doen en controle over wat ze mogen, zodat ze veilig en binnen de regels werken. adSCAILE: ons eigen framework waarmee je samen met AI-agents bouwt, geïntegreerd, veilig en traceerbaar, in cycli van twee tot vier dagen in plaats van sprints van weken. Je gebruikt deze tools dagelijks en helpt ze verder te ontwikkelen. adesso is bovendien Select Partner in het Claude Partner Network van Anthropic. En we blijven kritisch: niet alles hoeft met AI. De beste oplossing staat altijd voorop. En misschien wel het belangrijkste: de mensen Je komt terecht in een team waar vakmanschap, ondernemerschap en kennisdeling centraal staan. Je werkt met ervaren specialisten en groeit door in technische visie en in verantwoordelijkheid voor klantrelaties. We houden van collega's die nieuwsgierig zijn, kennis delen en elkaar verder helpen. Mensen die goed zijn in hun vak, maar ook plezier hebben in samenwerken. Je krijgt bij ons vertrouwen, verantwoordelijkheid en de vrijheid om ideeën daadwerkelijk uit te voeren. Wat krijg je van ons? €5.850–€7.150 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur 8% vakantiegeld Contract voor 32 tot 40 uur per week Een leaseauto of mobiliteitsvergoeding naar keuze, bovenop je salaris 27 vakantiedagen en 4 studiedagen €3.600 persoonlijk ontwikkelbudget per jaar en ruimte voor certificeringen Hybride werken met flexibele werktijden Goede pensioenregeling Doorgroeimogelijkheden in een special

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - German Speaking

At HappyRobot, there’s no role seniority or hierarchy — we operate as a team of builders. We execute, we build, we own, and we care deeply about our customers and their success. jobs.title: Machine Learning Compiler Engineer
jobs.jd:
About the position

We’re looking for compiler engineers to join a new ML Compilers Team at Jane Street. 

Machine learning is a critical pillar of our global business. Our ever-evolving trading environment serves as a unique, rapid-feedback platform for ML experimentation, allowing us to incorporate new ideas with relatively little friction. Our ML team is full of people with a shared love for the craft of software engineering, and for designing APIs and systems that are delightful to use.

ML compilers let us quickly turn research ideas and novel architectures into high-throughput training jobs and low-latency inference. To get the most out of our hardware resources and enable rapid model development and deployment, we are working to understand and improve the current ML compiler technologies and explore where it makes sense to build our own solutions. In this role, you would shape the development of our compiler stack.

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in.

About you

The ideal candidate has worked on an ML compiler in the past, but non-ML compiler experience is also valuable. Experience with any part of the stack is fine, be it high-level ML frameworks (PyTorch, Jax, TensorFlow), graph compilers (Inductor, XLA, TVM) or kernel DSLs (Triton, Helion, cuTile). You should understand how all those pieces fit together even if you are unfamiliar with specific parts. 

Some other things you might be excited about are:

  • Optimisations in ML compilers: algebraic rewriting, materialise vs recompute tradeoffs and fusion, equality saturation, scheduling languages, loop-level optimisation, autotuning
  • ML compiler frontends: graph capture, symbolic and dynamic shapes, control flow, automatic differentiation
  • GPU kernel programming and architecture: Triton, cuTile, CuTeDSL, CUDA, compute and memory hierarchies, programming with tensor cores
  • Compiler concepts: static analysis, intermediate representations like SSA and CFGs, instruction selection
  • ML inference: CUDA Graphs, KV caching, batching
  • ML training: Tensor/Sequence/Expert/Pipeline Parallelism, FSDP, NCCL, activation checkpointing
  • GPU debugging and optimisation: CUDA-GDB, Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute
  • Formal methods: proof assistants, automated theorem provers, agentic proof systems
  • Programming languages and DSL design: embedded DSLs, staging and metaprogramming, type systems, functional programming
  • Fluency in English is required

jobs.title: Founding Research Engineer or Research Scientist
jobs.jd: About Grubel Grubel is a research lab that builds AI for high-stakes knowledge work, starting with law. Legal matters require specialized expertise, and each one involves its own facts, practices, parties, and institutions. General-purpose AI applies the same system to every legal matter, varying only what goes into a limited context window. To meet the depth and diversity of legal work, we let every matter build its own AI: engineer the right data for the matter, adapt the model and agent to it, and track what improves. We combine the three into a matter-specific improvement loop that runs until the system delivers what the matter demands. Grubel was founded in 2026 by Moritz Hardt, director at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and formerly a UC Berkeley professor and Google Brain researcher; and Reinhard Heckel, professor of machine learning at the Technical University of Munich, on leave to build Grubel. The founding team includes engineers with PhDs in computer science and experience in foundation-model pretraining at Mistral and legal AI research at Thomson Reuters. The lab has offices in Munich and Tübingen. Point Nine led an oversubscribed pre-seed funding round with backing from leading AI researchers and founders, including Jeff Dean, Chris Ré, Ion Stoica, and Harvey co-founders Gabe Pereyra and Winston Weinberg. About the role We are looking for a Founding Research Engineer or Research Scientist to develop the methods and systems that make matter-specific AI possible. You will work on data curation, agent environment design, model adaptation, training, and evaluation. We do not draw a sharp boundary between research and engineering: everyone contributes substantial code, owns experiments end-to-end, builds systems, and helps turn successful methods into products. Research is empirical and engineering intensive. You will work directly with Grubel’s founders, engineers, legal experts, and enterprise partners. As an early member of the team, you will also help shape Grubel’s technical direction and research culture. What you’ll work on Developing, testing, and evaluating methods for adapting models and agents to individual legal matters Designing benchmarks and evaluation tasks for complex legal capabilities Developing data curation strategies for scaling from evaluation tasks to training tasks Building infrastructure for training, inference, experimentation, and evaluation Working with legal experts and enterprise partners to turn legal workflows into agentic workflows Turning successful research methods into reliable product capabilities You may be a good fit if You hold a master’s degree or PhD in machine learning, computer science, mathematics, or a related field, or have equivalent research or industry experience You have either a strong machine-learning research record or significant experience building large-scale machine-learning systems You have trained and evaluated language models or built agentic systems You are proactive, self-directed, and comfortable owning technically ambiguous problems You are curious about how legal work actually gets done and enjoy working with domain experts Particularly relevant experience Any of the following would be valuable, but we do not expect candidates to have all of them: LLM post-training, fine-tuning, or reinforcement learning experience Data curation, synthetic data, or human-in-the-loop data generation pipelines Evaluation harnesses and benchmark development Distributed training, inference, or experiment infrastructure Publications, open-source contributions, or deployed research systems Legal AI or another expert-intensive application domain Logistics Munich or Tübingen. We value working together in person, prefer candidates based near one of our offices, and expect at least one day per week in the office. We plan to establish a Zurich office in 2027. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Relevance
jobs.jd:

jobs.title: AI Engineer - RL Manipulation, RIVR
jobs.jd: Are you passionate about pushing the boundaries of what robots can do? Amazon is looking for a creative and driven Applied Scientist to help build intelligent robotic manipulation systems powered by reinforcement learning. In this role, you will research, design, and deploy machine learning solutions that enable robots to interact with the physical world in increasingly capable ways. You will tackle complex, ambiguous problems where textbook answers don't exist, working backwards from real-world needs to invent new approaches. Your work will directly influence how automation systems learn, adapt, and perform at Amazon's scale — and you will see your research come to life on real hardware. Key job responsibilities - Research and develop reinforcement learning methods for robotic manipulation, advancing the state of the art in sim-to-real transfer, contact-rich control, and adaptive grasping strategies. - Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning models and algorithms, leveraging deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow to train policies that generalize across varied manipulation tasks. - Build and maintain production-quality code that integrates scientific prototypes into larger robotics systems, making thoughtful tradeoffs between complexity, performance, and maintainability. - Collaborate with cross-functional engineering and science teams to define simulation requirements, validate model performance, and iterate on solutions informed by real-world hardware feedback. - Contribute to the team's scientific roadmap by identifying new research directions, mentoring fellow scientists, and publishing results at peer-reviewed venues when appropriate. A day in the life You might start your morning reviewing overnight training runs, analyzing reward curves and failure modes from your latest reinforcement learning experiments. After a quick sync with robotics engineers, you shift to refining a simulation environment to close a gap you spotted between sim and real performance. In the afternoon, you pair with a teammate to design a new evaluation framework, then wrap up by drafting a short write-up of your findings to share with the broader team. About the team Our team sits at the intersection of machine learning research and real-world robotics, focused on teaching robots to manipulate objects with precision and adaptability. We combine reinforcement learning, physics-based simulation, and hands-on hardware validation to deliver solutions that work beyond the lab. We value intellectual curiosity, collaborative problem-solving, and a shared commitment to turning ambitious research ideas into tangible impact. jobs.jd: Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too. We’re building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow’s machine learning open source and hosted tools. That includes counting cells to accelerate cancer research, improving construction site safety , digitizing floor plans , preserving coral reef populations , guiding drone flight , and much more . Our team is small relative to our impact, and we believe our user success is our success (not the inverse). A team member summarized: “Roboflow is a company full of giant brains and tiny egos.” We find software has a multiplier effect on all roles (not only product and engineering), so Roboflow employs developers across the company in design, sales, customer support, marketing, and beyond. We’re supported by great customers and investors, having raised over 63 million from Google Ventures, Y Combinator, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors. At the center of all of this is inference — one of our most important open source projects and the engine that runs computer vision models everywhere, from cloud GPUs to edge devices in the field. With that foundation, daily releases become routine, and we can say "yes" to far more contributions without ever lowering the bar — pushing back, by design, according to strictly defined review standards. You care about open source and the developers who depend on it. One of the best ways to stand out among other applicants is to write about something you've built with Roboflow, or to contribute to one of our open source projects — inference especially. What You'll Do Build and maintain inference , our flagship open source and commercial CV inference engine, keeping it healthy and high-quality as contribution volume scales. Design and grow a world-grounded, ever-expanding test suite that validates real build health across every target (standalone and on-platform), with the goal of nightly end-to-end runs across all of them. Exercise sharp judgment on when to merge fast and when to push back, and encode that judgment into the system itself. Streamline how new models get added to inference (the most fun part of the job) — making it dramatically faster and easier to bring the latest computer vision and ML models to our users. Teach and enable internal teams and customers. Keep our Field Engineers and Support team a step ahead so they can self-serve and go deeper, and help customers get the full value of the product. Contribute to and grow the broader open source community around the project. This direct connection keeps our development roadmaps relevant, speeds up solution delivery, and strengthens our ability to co-innovate across the region. As part of our Customer Engineering function,, you will design production-ready, repeatable architectural blueprints and lead technical scoping alongside strategic customers and technology partners. Your mission is to eliminate technical and organizational friction to establish modern, enterprise-grade Kubernetes container systems as the preferred platform for high-scale application and AI workloads. In this team, career growth and seniority are defined purely by your technical competence, architectural depth, and ability to deliver end-to-end solutions autonomously in highly ambiguous environments while mentoring technically AI/ML engineering colleagues. There is no expectation of team management or administrative coordination; your progression is driven entirely by engineering design impact, advisory leadership and your ability to coach and develop junior team members. What You Will Do: Enterprise-Minded Blueprinting: Design and document comprehensive, production-ready system architecture blueprints and reference topologies. Ecosystem & Partner Integration: Collaborate with external technology ecosystems (such as chip manufacturers, independent software vendors, and regional system integrators) to design and validate joint-architecture solutions. The Elastic Security Endpoint Protections team researches, designs, and builds the visibility and prevention capabilities at the core of Elastic Defend, our endpoint and SIEM security solution. What You Will Be Doing

  • Research emerging attacker techniques and turn them into shipped protections. Study real-world tradecraft across in-memory threats, injection, credential theft, ransomware, and kernel tampering, then design protections that hold up against an adversary actively trying to defeat them.

  • Develop production code that runs everywhere. Write performant, stable C/C++ that executes on millions of endpoints, where a memory leak or a few milliseconds of overhead is a customer-visible problem.
  • Reverse engineer malware and study evasion. Learn how attackers bypass endpoint security controls in the wild, and feed that understanding directly into the protections you design and harden.
  • Own efficacy end to end. Review customer telemetry at fleet scale, investigate false positives and performance regressions, and establish mitigation strategies. Shipping the feature is the beginning of the job, not the end.
  • Extend protection parity across platforms. Bring the depth we have on Windows to macOS and Linux, and support new hardware architectures as they reach the enterprise.

  • Deep operating system internals knowledge, in both kernel and user mode, deep enough to reason about undocumented behavior and find security-relevant structures nobody has written about yet. Windows depth is what we need most, with macOS or Linux depth close behind.
  • In-depth reverse engineering and malware analysis experience, and comfort with the tooling that makes hard binaries readable.

  • A collaborative mentality and an eagerness to learn new skills, new platforms, and emerging technologies.
